evidence.claim: Descartes markets Global Trade Intelligence solutions covering import/export data, duty and tariff data, export compliance, product classification, denied-party screening, sanctions/restricted-party list content, trade analytics, and supply-chain risk/compliance workflows.

A February 2025 Descartes release described technology innovations in its global trade intelligence software suite and stated that combining HS-based trade data with legislation/regulation content can support product, party, and shipment compliance risk assessment.
evidence.source_title: Descartes Showcases Global Trade Intelligence Technology Innovations

evidence.claim: UL Solutions states that its independent third-party testing, certification, and validation services help finished goods meet compliance requirements and buyer/retailer demands, including product sustainability across supply chains.

ICF disclosed Department of Labor ILAB contracts to provide research and advisory services supporting efforts to combat forced and child labor, including work to more closely trace sources of forced and child labor in global supply chains.
evidence.source_title: U.S. Department of Labor Awards ICF $34 Million in New Research Services Contracts

evidence.claim: ICF reported Q1 2026 government-client revenue of $291.2 million and highlighted technology modernization, data analytics, rulemaking support, environmental compliance, and Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency data-management work among government awards.

FiscalNote markets global policy and market intelligence products across public policy, regulations, geopolitical risk, government affairs, elections, ESG, and supply-chain-related content categories.
evidence.source_title: Global Policy and Market Intelligence | FiscalNote

evidence.claim: CNAS argued in May 2026 that the defense industrial base remains shallow and that DoD and prime contractors often lack visibility beyond direct or tier-two suppliers, supporting demand for supply-chain illumination and mapping.

The Defense Management Institute describes supply-chain illumination as an analytical process for transparency into supply-chain entities, products, parts, and raw materials to identify risk and enable proactive mitigation.
evidence.source_title: Supply Chain Illumination in the Department of Defense - Defense Management Institute

evidence.claim: Dun & Bradstreet was excluded from the candidate list because Clearlake completed its acquisition on August 26, 2025, after which D&B became privately held and its stock ceased trading and was delisted from the NYSE.

memory_update.text: DSGX is the cleanest public mid-cap candidate found for the trade-compliance and tariff/sanctions/data portion of the supply-chain visibility node.
ULS is a large-cap reference name for TIC/certification exposure; keep as context anchor, but later layers should test whether policy-linked compliance is material versus generic testing demand.
ICFI is an underfollowed small-cap government-services candidate with evidence of forced-labor supply-chain tracing and policy implementation exposure, but not a pure software/data play.

NOTE is a speculative micro-cap exception for policy/regulatory intelligence exposure; must be heavily filtered for liquidity, listing status, balance-sheet risk, and real supply-chain-compliance use cases.

Several highly relevant pure-play supply-chain illumination vendors appear private rather than public, including Interos, Exiger, Everstream Analytics, and Altana; public-market mapping may therefore require second-order proxies.
Dun & Bradstreet would have been a strong supplier-risk/data candidate, but it is no longer US-listed after the completed Clearlake acquisition and NYSE delisting in August 2025.

node: Supply-chain visibility, traceability, compliance, and sourcing-resilience tools
summary: Expanded the universe around a narrow policy-linked data/compliance chokepoint: trade-compliance software, certification/testing, government supply-chain analytics, and policy/regulatory intelligence. The best-fit underfollowed lane is not defense primes or obvious AI software, but mid/small-cap companies whose products help customers prove supplier origin, manage sanctions/export controls, validate product compliance, trace forced-labor exposure, or modernize government supply-chain data. This pass is research-only and does not imply buy/sell action.
